prompt: I'm about to start on the distributed query view work. Explain to a newcomer, as briefly as you can, what it changes about who does what between Proxy, QueryCoord, StreamingNode and QueryNode and why, what a DataView version and a QueryView version are, how a query view moves through its states, how much of it serves production traffic today, and where each part is written down.
key: The design is docs/design-docs/design_docs/qviews/README.md (state machines from #51887, 2026-08-11; revised to 2026-11-02), with its sub-documents beside it. Why: putting today's delegator on StreamingNode would route every segment load/release, delete apply, query and result through it, making it a compute- and IO-heavy global bottleneck. So QueryCoord manages sealed-segment Load/Release directly and generates the globally complete query view; StreamingNode only accepts view updates and serves the incremental (growing) part; Proxy queries in two phases, getting a shard-level plan (MVCC, optimizations, the view version) from StreamingNode, then sending it to StreamingNode and the designated QueryNodes and doing all reduce itself, retrying on node failure or view invalidation; QueryNodes subscribe to delete data from StreamingNode and apply it themselves. DataView (data_view.md) is the complete, non-duplicate loadable sealed-segment set, versioned per collection as (streaming_version, compact_version): streaming_version moves only on the flush atomic txn, compact_version on every other membership change (compaction, import, L0, drop, truncate). A QueryView version is (DataVersion, query_version) at ShardOnReplica level, query_version moving on load-level redistribution. Coord leads a state machine: Preparing → Ready → Up → Down → Dropping → Dropped, with Preparing → Unrecoverable → Dropping on error, at most one Preparing view per node (query_view_state_machine.md); an SN serving lease delays Up → Down while in use (query_view_lease.md). Today it does not serve production traffic: SN plan/execution and an injectable query client exist, but production Proxy routing is not switched and the new Coordinator runtime is not activated; the query/ documents (query_plan, query_client, query_execution, segment_pruning) and the SN WAL view (wal/streamingnode_vchannel_wal_view.md) carry the rest.

sources.quote: StreamingNode would become a compute-intensive and IO-intensive global bottleneck node
QueryCoord directly manages all SealedSegment Load/Release operations.

Proxy uses a two-phase query approach — it generates a query plan on StreamingNode, then sends the query plan to designated QueryNodes to complete the query, and performs all distributed Reduce operations itself.
After LoadSegment, QueryNode proactively subscribes to the corresponding Delete data from StreamingNode and applies Delete data on its own.
They do not switch production Proxy routing or activate the new Coordinator runtime.
Incremented only by the flush atomic txn (PrepareFlush) for the growing-to-sealed query handoff.
The query view version number is at the ShardOnReplica level
The query view maintains consistency across Coord / QueryNode / StreamingNode, with Coord as the leader.
Normal flow: Preparing → Ready → Up → Down → Dropping → Dropped

rubric.criterion: Why: StreamingNode as delegator would become a global compute and IO bottleneck

Who does what: QueryCoord owns sealed load/release and the complete view; Proxy plans on StreamingNode, executes on StreamingNode and QueryNodes and reduces itself; QueryNodes subscribe to and apply deletes
DataView is versioned (streaming_version, compact_version) per collection, and a QueryView version adds a query version per shard on a replica
The state machine, Coord-led: Preparing, Ready, Up, Down, Dropping, Dropped, with Unrecoverable as the error path
Says it is not yet serving production traffic: Proxy routing is not switched and the new Coordinator runtime is not active
Names the documents (qviews/README.md and its sub-documents such as data_view.md and query_view_state_machine.md), and is brief and says nothing false
Names where the reason comes from — a document, a note or a file of this project — rather than asserting it; an answer that gives a reason with no source does not earn this.
